advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make `_has_remote` failure treat the checkout as not-provably-complete (allow) rather than falling through to a refusal, matching its docstring.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/link_revert.py:48: `except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — an unprobeable checkout is simply not provably complete`
`if _has_remote(code_root):` at link_revert.py:122 — False skips the block and reaches the refusal `return` at 128
run_git docstring: '``timeout`` (when set) lets :class:`subprocess.TimeoutExpired` propagate' (gitutil.py:121) — a hung `git remote` raises, is caught, and yields the refusal path
advisory.finding: `_has_remote` returns False on ANY exception (including `run_git`'s `TimeoutExpired` on a hung `git remote`), and a False return skips the refresh block and falls through to REFUSE. An unprobeable/hung checkout thus produces a refusal — contradicting the function's own docstring ('an unprobeable checkout is simply not provably complete', i.e. absence unproven → allow) and reintroducing the escalation-forcing refusal the change exists to eliminate.
advisory.suggested_fix: Distinguish probe failure from a genuine no-remote result: on exception/timeout, treat the checkout as unverifiable and allow the link (return None) rather than proceeding to refuse.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Capture `git_started_ns` after `log_argv` is fully built (or time `upstream_branch_refs` separately) so the metric reflects only the log walk.
evidence: src/rebar/_engine_support/commit_impact.py:238: `git_started_ns = time.monotonic_ns() if metrics is not None else 0`
upstream_branch_refs runs two subprocess.run calls (commit_impact.py:175-193) inside that timed window
advisory.finding: When `include_upstream=True`, the git-history-read metric `git_history_read_ms` now also covers the two extra `git symbolic-ref`/`for-each-ref` subprocess invocations made by `upstream_branch_refs`, because `git_started_ns` is captured before argv construction which invokes `upstream_branch_refs`. The metric name still implies it measures only the log walk.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test: repo_with_history + a reachable empty upstream remote (`git remote add origin <bare-empty-repo>`) + a commitless target still raises RebarError (refusal after a successful refresh).
evidence: link_revert.py:122-131: `if _has_remote(code_root): / if not _refresh_remote_refs(code_root): return None / found = _scan(...) / if found is None or found: return None` then `return (f"target ticket '{target_id}' has no commit referencing it ...")` — the refusal is reachable ONLY when a remote exists, the refresh succeeds, and the rescan is still empty.

The `_bare_repo` fixture (tests/unit/...:28-36) and `repo_with_history` (lines 39-44) never run `git remote add`, so `test_caused_by_to_a_commitless_target_is_refused_and_writes_nothing` (line 83) hits `_has_remote()==False`.

The only remote-configured new tests are line 300 (`_git(repo, "remote", "add", "origin", str(upstream))` where upstream HAS the culprit -> allow) and line 315 (`str(tmp_path / "definitely-not-a-repo")` -> refresh fails -> allow).
search for `refresh` in the test file returns no matches; no test asserts a RebarError after a successful refresh.

ABSENCE rationale: a regression inverting `_refresh_remote_refs`'s return, or making the post-refresh refusal unreachable, would make every reachable-remote checkout ALLOW a commitless caused_by target and no test would fail.
blocking.finding: No test covers the refuse-after-successful-refresh path: a checkout WITH a reachable remote where the fetch succeeds but the target is still genuinely commitless must raise a refusal. Every new test that configures a remote ends in an ALLOW verdict (commit found upstream, or the remote is unreachable), and the one existing refusal test uses repo_with_history which has no remote configured, so it exercises only the `_has_remote() is False` branch.
scenarios: A server-side clone with a reachable origin that genuinely never shipped a commit for the target — the guard must still refuse but a regression could silently allow it.
blocking.suggested_fix: Add a test mirroring test_a_commit_present_only_upstream_is_consulted_before_refusing but with the upstream lacking any commit referencing the culprit, asserting `pytest.raises(rebar.RebarError)` and that no caused_by edge is written.
